citation.title: Data-driven topology optimization of spinodoid metamaterials with seamlessly tunable anisotropy
citation.authors: Li Zheng, Siddhant Kumar, Dennis M. Kochmann
citation.venue: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For the first cantilever benchmark, the spinodoid design has compliance 0.5602 versus 0.5299 for classical SIMP, so its reported compliance is higher in that comparison.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Appendix B, Table B.1: a single FEM microscale homogenization takes about 5 minutes (300 s), versus 0.001 s for one DNN stiffness prediction, yielding 300,000× for that subtask only; it is not a whole-optimization speedup and hardware differs.
claim.alternatives: Section 5.2.2 reports 8.35% lower compliance than SIMP for the L-shape; later benchmarks report 4.88% and 1.27% improvements. Appendix B compares single-stiffness prediction times.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP for homogeneous isotropic solid, penalty p=4, filter radius 0.075 and final thresholding; FEM homogenization for microscale stiffness subtask (Section 5.2, Appendix B)
baseline.implementation: In-house C++ FEM for homogenization; SIMP implementation not stated (Appendix B, Section 5.2)
baseline.hardware_classical: FEM homogenization: 16 MPI cores on ETH Euler IV cluster, two 18-core 2.7 GHz Xeon Gold 6150 CPUs, 192 GB RAM; SIMP hardware not stated (Table B.1)
baseline.hardware_ml: DNN prediction on CPU without parallelization; four 12-core 2.2 GHz Xeon E5-2650 CPUs and 256 GB RAM system; benchmark runs on CPU (Table B.1)
baseline.problem_size: Cantilever 64×48×2 grid with linear tetrahedra; L-shape 22,060 tetrahedral elements and 110,300 design variables (Sections 5.2.1–5.2.2)
baseline.classical_time: About 5 minutes per FEM microscale homogenization; whole SIMP benchmark runtime not stated (Table B.1)
baseline.ml_time: 0.001 seconds per DNN stiffness prediction; full benchmarks I–IV take 3, 3.5, 4.5 and 8 hours respectively (Table B.1)
baseline.training_time: 10 minutes for DNN training on CPU; adapted from prior work (Table B.1)
baseline.data_generation_cost: 19,170 FEM homogenization training pairs; about 5 minutes per stiffness computation stated, but aggregate generation time not stated (Section 5.1, Table B.1)
baseline.quality_metric: Optimized macroscale compliance at average relative density 0.5 in cantilever and L-shape (Section 5.2, Figures 7c and 10c)
baseline.quality_gap: Cantilever: spinodoid 5.602×10^-1 versus SIMP 5.299×10^-1 compliance (Figure 7c), about 5.7% higher [inferred]. L-shape: reported 8.35% lower than SIMP (Section 5.2.2).

R1.evidence: Section 5.2.1, Figure 7c: selected outcome compares compliance, not whole-design speed.

R2.evidence: Section 5.2.1: selected SIMP comparison is quality-only; the Appendix B timing is a microscale stiffness subtask on different hardware.

R3.evidence: Section 5.2.1: selected outcome is quality-only, so speed cost accounting is not applicable to it.

R4.evidence: Sections 4–5 and Figure 7c: macroscale compliance uses FE with DNN-predicted homogenized microstructural stiffness; the returned spatially varying microstructure is not FE-tested at full resolution (Section 5.2.1).

notes: The abstract's speed language compares DNN stiffness prediction against microscale FEM, whereas the first quantitative optimization-level classical comparison is Figure 7c. The compared material design spaces differ: spatially varying spinodoids versus homogeneous isotropic SIMP.
